title: Cooperative scanback prefetch and writeback coalescer for blocked KV pageflow
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Overview:
This ticket proposes a blocked/paged KV cache runtime component called the 'scanback prefetcher' paired with a writeback coalescer to reduce GPU OOMs and tail latency under continuous batching workloads. The design focuses on cooperative CPU/GPU prefetching, compact writeback windows, and a soft-throttle mechanism that ties batch admission to anticipated residency budgets. Key goals: reduce PCIe read spikes, control host-stage residency, and preserve 99th-percentile latency SLOs while supporting oversubscription for bursty workloads.

What this implements (high level):
- Blocked pageflow: KV entries are grouped into fixed-size blocks (default 2MB aligned to slab boundaries) that are the unit of residency and transfer.
- Cooperative scanback prefetch: when a request stream references cache misses, the prefetcher performs a bounded scanback from the token access point using a spectral heat estimate to decide adjacent block prefetches. The algorithm biases toward recent tokens (temporal hotness) and cross-request affinity (token affinity lanes).
- Writeback coalescer: dirty/modified blocks are batched into time-windowed writeback units to host memory (or NVMe) to amortize PCIe overhead and avoid frequent small evictions that amplify read amplification.
- Host staging ring with residency budgets: a ring buffer on host memory for prefetched blocks, with a configurable residency budget per GPU; eviction from host staging is LRU with a hotset-aware grace window.
- Backpressure integration: admission controller adjusts batch size/batching delay when projected GPU residency would exceed the configured budget; this integrates with continuous batching so we gracefully tradeoff throughput versus memory safety.

Implementation details and heuristics:
- Block size and alignment: default 2MB blocks chosen after empirical tests showing optimal PCIe throughput vs read amplification. Blocks align with slab allocator so block boundary splits are rare.
- Spectral heat estimate: maintain a lightweight per-token exponential decay counter (alpha=0.35) and a per-block sampled histogram. Prefetch weight for a neighboring block is proportional to the ratio of hotness between candidate block and average workload hotness.
- Bounded scan depth: configurable (default 3 blocks). Avoids unbounded prefetching in long sequences.
- Prefetch concurrency limiter: token-prefetch ops are funneled through a small pool to avoid PCIe saturation; default concurrency 8 per-GPU.
- Coalesced writebacks: dirty blocks accumulate for a configurable window (default 50ms) and then flushed together; the coalescer groups contiguous blocks into a single DMA where possible.
- GPU pinning for active batches: during request execution, blocks required by in-flight batches are pinned for the duration of the batch and released in controlled windows to avoid micro-oscillation of residency.
- Emergency OOM path: if projected residency + inflight > hard_limit, we escalate: (1) reject new low-priority batches with 429-like error, (2) fallback to a smaller model variant if applicable, (3) perform a prioritized eviction sweep using a hotness-aware heuristic.

Observability and metrics:
- New metrics: block_prefetch_rate, host_stage_utilization, coalesced_writeback_latency, prefetch_miss_ratio, pin_duration_histogram, admission_throttle_events.
- Dashboards: KV heatmap (block-level) and host staging occupancy over time.
- Alerts: sustained host_stage_utilization > 80% for 5m, coalesced_writeback_latency > 200ms, admission_throttle_events spike > 0.5% of requests.

Trade-offs considered:
- Larger blocks improve DMA efficiency but increase read amplification for sparse accesses. We chose conservative 2MB default with config knob per deployment.
- Aggressive prefetch reduces miss latency but can cause host-stage pressure; bounded scan depth and spectral weighting are used to limit waste.
- Coalescing writebacks adds flush latency for durability, but our target workloads are read-dominated and tolerate short coalescing windows.

Testing and validation plan:
- Microbench harness: synthetic traces imitating chatty and long-context LLM workloads; run permutations of block size, scan depth, writeback window.
- Canary plan: staged canary that starts at 2% traffic on a dedicated Dedicated capacity pool (canary-2%) for 72 hours, then 10% for 48 hours, watch for OOMs and latency regressions.
- Benchmarks: measure median/99th generation latency, throughput, and per-token cost under 1x/3x/10x load.

Rollout and ops playbook:
- Default OFF for hosted runtime; enabled by feature flag per-customer for Dedicated/Private.
- Must provide quick kill switch on admission controller and host-stage cap adjustments.
- Runbook steps for persistent host staging growth: (1) scale down prefetch concurrency, (2) shrink scan depth, (3) increase writeback coalescing frequency, (4) if unresolved, temporarily enforce aggressive admission throttling.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc (detailed rationale + microbench results): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Cooperative+Scanback+Prefetch+Design
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5234
- Grafana dashboard (kv paging heatmap): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/kv/kv-paging-heatmap

Longer-term ideas (out of scope for this ticket):
- Machine-learned prefetch policy trained on production access patterns.
- NVMe-backed resident tier with prioritized promotion/growth.
- Cross-GPU shared host-stage with multi-GPU cohesive eviction.
